summary: 1956 Georgia Forestry Commission steel tower in Colquitt, Miller County; staffed until the late 1980s, now kept for radio and emergency use; NHLR-registered 2006.

facts.design: 99-foot International Stacy steel tower with a metal 7 by 7 foot cab and a catwalk

access.note: On the grounds of a Georgia Forestry Commission station. The Register says it is kept for radio and emergency use. No public visiting arrangement appears in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No visiting details in the sources read. Ask the Georgia Forestry Commission before going to the station.

events.note: Constructed by the Georgia Forestry Commission in Colquitt

evidence.supports: built in 1956 by the Georgia Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: The Miller County Fire Tower was constructed by the Georgia Forestry Commission in 1956

evidence.supports: location in the Town of Colquitt, Miller County
99-foot International Stacy tower, metal 7 by 7 foot cab, catwalk
evidence.quote: The 99’ International Stacy tower with metal 7’x7’ cab is unusual in that it has a catwalk

evidence.supports: staffed until the late 1980s; now maintained for emergency detection and radio for the forestry station
evidence.quote: Staffed until the late 1980s, it is maintained for emergency detection and radio communications for the forestry station on the site

evidence.supports: administered by the Georgia Forestry Commission
1956 build; 99-foot steel tower with 7 x 7 cab (maker spelled International-Stacey)
evidence.quote: 1956: A 99-foot International-Stacey steel tower with a 7 x 7 cab was erected.

evidence.supports: listed under Miller County, Georgia Forestry Commission

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register spells the maker International Stacy; Forest Lookouts spells it International-Stacey. Both describe the same 99-foot steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot cab, so only the spelling differs.

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The Register is the main source; Forest Lookouts repeats the 1956 build and design in one line. No fire history, no current condition check and no visiting information were found. The brief's record matches the Register (built 1956, registered 2006, elevation 44 m), so no corrections are proposed. The 99 ft height is converted to 30.2 m. Standing and maintained are taken from the Register's present-tense text, which is undated.
